aiOverview.content: After storm damage, safely inspect your roof from the ground for missing shingles, leaks, or debris, and document everything with photos for insurance. Hire a reputable local contractor for repairs, which may include replacing shingles, fixing flashing, or emergency tarping to prevent further water damage. Immediate Actions After Storm Damage: Safety First: Stay off the roof. Inspect from the ground or using binoculars. Document Damage: Take photos and videos of all damaged areas, including missing shingles, dents, and damaged gutters. Temporary Repairs: Use a tarp to cover damaged areas to prevent water from entering the home. Contact Insurance: Notify your homeowners insurance provider immediately to file a claim. Hire Local Professionals: Choose a licensed and insured, local roofing contractor. Avoid "storm chasers" who travel to affected areas. This video explains how to identify roof damage after a storm:1mThe Roofing ChannelYouTube• Sep 30, 2021 1m Common Storm Roof Repairs: Shingle Replacement: Replacing blown-off, torn, or broken shingles, which may involve loosening surrounding shingles and applying new sealant. Flashing Repair: Resealing or replacing damaged flashing around chimneys, vents, and skylights. Attic Inspection: Checking for leaks, wet insulation, and musty odors. Structural Repair: Repairing damaged roof decking, rafters, or trusses. This video demonstrates how to repair shingle damage caused by a storm:59sPrecision RoofingYouTube• Dec 17, 2024 59s What to Look For: Roofing Materials: Missing shingles, granules in gutters, or dents from hail. Inside: Water stains on ceilings, wet insulation, or daylight visible through the roof in the attic. Structural: Sagging areas, damaged vents, or damaged chimney caps. Repair costs vary significantly depending on the damage, with average repairs ranging from around $2,655 to $21,974.
